title: Decision Making and Eligibility
summary: The 'given these rules, does this candidate qualify, get referred, or get rejected' question. How to read a rules block with exceptions, apply it case by case, and use the 'data inadequate' verdict when a required fact is missing.
learningObjectives: Extract the core conditions, the referral conditions, and the rejection conditions from a rules block.
Check a candidate against every core condition before considering an exception.
Apply exactly one referral route when a single core condition is narrowly missed.
Return 'data inadequate' when a fact needed to decide is not given.

blocks.title: Rules, candidates, verdicts
blocks.markdown:
You are given a **rules block** — the conditions for some outcome (a loan, a seat, a promotion), with a few **exception clauses** that send a near-miss candidate to a named authority. Then several candidate profiles, each to be given one verdict:

- **Qualifies / selected** — every condition met.
- **Referred to X** — exactly one condition narrowly missed, and an exception names X.
- **Rejected / not eligible** — a condition missed with no exception for it.
- **Data inadequate** — a fact needed to decide is not stated.

Read the rules once in full before looking at any candidate.
searchKeywords: rules block conditions for an outcome exception clauses near miss to a named authority
verdicts qualifies referred rejected data inadequate
read the rules once in full before looking at any candidate

blocks.title: Working a candidate
blocks.markdown:
1. **List the core conditions** as a checklist (age band, income floor, score floor, tenure, …).
2. **Tick each one for the candidate.** Stop reading exceptions until the checklist is done.
3. **All ticked → qualifies.**
4. **Exactly one missed → look for an exception** that covers *that* condition and *this* candidate's numbers. If one fits, the verdict is the referral it names. If none fits, **rejected**.
5. **Two or more missed → rejected** (referrals cover a single narrow miss only).
6. **A needed fact absent → data inadequate**, but only if the candidate would otherwise pass or be referrable — a candidate already rejected on a stated fact stays rejected.
searchKeywords: list the core conditions as a checklist tick each one stop reading exceptions until done
all ticked qualifies exactly one missed look for an exception covering that condition
two or more missed rejected needed fact absent data inadequate

blocks.title: When to say 'data inadequate'
blocks.markdown:
Use it only when a fact you **need in order to decide** is missing.

- If the candidate already fails a stated condition, the missing fact does not matter — **rejected**.
- If every stated fact passes and only one required fact is unstated, you cannot confirm 'qualifies' — **data inadequate**.
- If a fact is missing but an exception would apply either way, decide by the exception.

Do not treat 'not mentioned' as 'condition met' or as 'condition failed'. It is its own verdict.
searchKeywords: data inadequate only when a fact needed to decide is missing
candidate already fails a stated condition missing fact does not matter rejected
every stated fact passes one required fact unstated cannot confirm qualifies

blocks.title: Worked example: personal loan
blocks.markdown:
**Rules.** A personal loan is granted if the applicant: (i) is aged 23 to 58 inclusive; (ii) has monthly net income of at least ₹30,000; (iii) has been in the current job for at least 2 years; (iv) has a credit score of at least 700.

*Exceptions.* (A) If (i), (ii), (iii) are met but the score is 650–699, refer to the **Credit Manager**. (B) If (i), (ii), (iv) are met but current-job tenure is 1–2 years while income is at least ₹60,000, refer to the **Branch Head**.

| Candidate | Facts | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rahul | 30 yrs, ₹45,000, 4 yrs in job, score 720 | **Loan granted** — all four met. |
| Meena | 40 yrs, ₹35,000, 3 yrs, score 680 | **Refer to Credit Manager** — only the score is missed, in the 650–699 band (exception A). |
| Sam | 26 yrs, ₹70,000, 1.5 yrs, score 710 | **Refer to Branch Head** — only tenure missed, income ≥ ₹60,000 (exception B). |
| Priya | 22 yrs, ₹50,000, 3 yrs, score 730 | **Rejected** — age below 23, and no exception covers the age condition. |
searchKeywords: worked example personal loan rules age income tenure credit score exceptions credit manager branch head
Rahul all met granted Meena score 680 refer credit manager Sam tenure income branch head
Priya age below 23 no exception rejected

blocks.title: Worked example: trainee recruitment
blocks.markdown:
**Rules.** Select a management trainee if the candidate: (i) is a graduate with at least 60% marks; (ii) is aged 21 to 28 as on 1 January 2026; (iii) scored at least 50 in the written test; (iv) can join within 30 days.

*Exceptions.* (A) If (ii), (iii), (iv) are met but marks are 55–59%, refer to the **Selection Committee**. (B) If (i), (iii), (iv) are met but age is 29 or 30, refer to the **General Manager**.

| Candidate | Facts | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kiran | graduate 72%, 24 yrs, test 65, joins in 20 days | **Selected** — all four met. |
| Rohit | graduate 58%, 25 yrs, test 55, joins in 15 days | **Refer to Selection Committee** — only marks missed, in the 55–59% band (exception A). |
| Sneha | graduate 68%, 30 yrs, test 60, joins in 10 days | **Refer to General Manager** — only age missed, at 30 (exception B). |
| Vikas | graduate 65%, 26 yrs, test 58, joining date not stated | **Data inadequate** — (i), (ii), (iii) pass; joining time is required and unstated. |
| Asha | graduate 62%, 24 yrs, test 45 | **Rejected** — written score below 50, no exception for it. |
searchKeywords: worked example trainee recruitment graduate marks age written test joining exceptions selection committee general manager
Kiran selected Rohit 58 percent selection committee Sneha age 30 general manager
Vikas joining date not stated data inadequate Asha test 45 rejected

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.markdown:
- **Jumping to an exception** before checking every core condition — an exception applies only when exactly one core condition is missed.
- **Stacking two exceptions** for a candidate who misses two conditions. That candidate is rejected.
- **Reading a band wrongly** — 'score 650–699' does not include 649 or 700.
- **Treating 'not mentioned' as met.** If a needed fact is absent and the rest pass, the verdict is data inadequate.
- **Applying an exception whose own sub-conditions fail** — exception B needs income ≥ ₹60,000, not just short tenure.
searchKeywords: decision making mistakes jumping to an exception before checking every core condition
stacking two exceptions candidate misses two conditions rejected reading a band wrongly
treating not mentioned as met applying an exception whose sub conditions fail

blocks.title: Quick revision
blocks.markdown:
- Build a checklist of the core conditions; tick each for the candidate before reading exceptions.
- All ticked → qualifies. Exactly one missed → the referral named by a matching exception, else rejected. Two or more missed → rejected.
- An exception applies only if its own sub-conditions (income floor, marks band, age band) also hold.
- A required fact left unstated, with everything else passing → data inadequate; a candidate already failing a stated condition stays rejected.
- Read number bands exactly — endpoints matter.

all ticked qualifies one missed referral or rejected two missed rejected
exception needs its own sub conditions required fact unstated data inadequate read bands exactly

blocks.title: Practice
blocks.markdown:
Use the **personal loan** rules from the first worked example: aged 23–58 inclusive; net income ≥ ₹30,000; current-job tenure ≥ 2 years; credit score ≥ 700. Exception A — (i),(ii),(iii) met but score 650–699 → Credit Manager. Exception B — (i),(ii),(iv) met but tenure 1–2 years and income ≥ ₹60,000 → Branch Head.

Give each candidate one verdict (granted / refer to Credit Manager / refer to Branch Head / rejected / data inadequate) with a one-line reason.

1. Deepak — 35 yrs, ₹32,000, 5 yrs in job, score 705.
2. Farah — 45 yrs, ₹28,000, 6 yrs, score 780.
3. Gita — 50 yrs, ₹40,000, 3 yrs, score 690.
4. Harish — 27 yrs, ₹65,000, 1 year 8 months in job, score 712.
5. Irfan — 60 yrs, ₹90,000, 20 yrs, score 800; states he will not add a co-applicant.
6. Jaya — 29 yrs, ₹55,000, score 720; her current-job tenure is not stated.
7. Karan — 33 yrs, ₹58,000, 1.5 yrs, score 720.

flashcards.front: Before applying any exception clause, what must you do?
flashcards.back: Check the candidate against every core condition. An exception applies only when exactly one core condition is narrowly missed.
flashcards.explanation: Reading exceptions early causes wrong referrals.

flashcards.front: A candidate misses two core conditions. What is the verdict?
flashcards.back: Rejected. Referral exceptions cover a single narrow miss only — you cannot stack two of them.
flashcards.explanation: No exception is written for two simultaneous misses.

flashcards.front: When is 'data inadequate' the right verdict?
flashcards.back: When every stated fact passes and exactly one fact required to decide is missing. If a stated fact already fails, it is 'rejected' instead.

flashcards.front: An exception says 'tenure 1-2 years but income ≥ ₹60,000 → Branch Head'. A candidate has short tenure but income ₹50,000. Apply it?
flashcards.back: No. The exception's own sub-condition (income ≥ ₹60,000) fails, so the exception does not apply — the candidate is rejected.
flashcards.explanation: Every part of the exception must hold.

flashcards.front: The rule needs a score of at least 700; the exception covers 650-699. What is the verdict for a score of exactly 700? For 649?
flashcards.back: 700 meets the core rule (that condition is ticked). 649 is outside the exception band, so if that is the only condition context, the exception cannot rescue it.

flashcards.front: List the four possible verdicts for a candidate.
flashcards.back: Qualifies/granted; referred to a named authority; rejected; data inadequate.
